preamble: Debuccalization of the aspirated velar stop [kʰ] to the glottal fricative [h] removes the oral closure and keeps only the aspiration. In Maharashtri Prakrit every intervocalic aspirated stop, kh included, was reduced to h (Sanskrit mukha > Prakrit muha > Hindi mũh). In Cantonese the Middle Chinese aspirated initial kʰ- (the 溪 initial) became h- before unrounded vowels, and the vernacular layer of Hakka shows the same outcome.

examples.note: Intervocalic aspirated stops lost their oral closure and left h; Hindi mukh is a later tatsama borrowing.
The Middle Chinese aspirated velar initial became h- before unrounded vowels; Mandarin keeps a stop (kāi).
The vernacular reading has h-, while the literary reading keeps the aspirated stop.

sources: Pischel, R. (1900). Grammatik der Prākrit-Sprachen. Trübner. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783111700007
